about: Shared test vectors for live plan edits, protocol version 1. The website (src/lib/live/ops.ts, client-state.ts) and the game's Java engine both run every vector here and must pass all of them. Change a rule and this file changes with it.

THE MODEL. A plan is a JSON object. The arrays named in 'collections' (below) are collections of things, each a JSON object with a string 'id'. Every other top-level field of the plan is meta, including arrays not in the list. An absent collection, or one that is not an array (null, a string), equals an empty one.

OPS. {o:'put',c,id,v} inserts or replaces the whole thing: a new id is appended to the end of the collection (the collection is created when absent); an existing id is replaced in place; the stored thing always has id = the op's id. {o:'patch',c,id,f,d?} sets every top-level field named in f to its value, THEN deletes every field named in d; it never sets or deletes 'id'; it does nothing when the thing (or its collection) is absent. A patch replaces a field's whole value (no deep merge). {o:'del',c,id} removes the thing; nothing when it is absent. {o:'meta',f,d?} sets then deletes top-level plan fields; names of collections in f or d are ignored. A batch is a list of ops applied in order; later writes win. null is an ordinary value; an absent field is absent (a delete is always a name in d, never null).

EQUALITY ('jsonEqual'): numbers by value (1 equals 1.0 equals 1.00e0), objects by key set and values regardless of key order, arrays element by element in order, strings by exact UTF-16 code units, null only equals null, true/false by value. PLAN EQUALITY ('plansEqual'): every meta field jsonEqual (absent equals absent only), and for every collection the same things by id regardless of order, each pair jsonEqual; an absent collection equals an empty one. Ids are unique inside a collection.

DIFF of before -> after: for each collection in 'collections' order, a put for each thing only in after and a patch for each thing in both with any top-level field different (both in after's order), and a del for each thing only in before (in before's order). A patch's f holds each field added or changed (the after value, whole), its d the removed field names sorted by UTF-16 code units (Java's String.compareTo), and d is left out when empty; f is always present, possibly {}. Then one meta op, built the same way over the plan's top-level non-collection fields, only when something changed. The batch is ordered: every put (collections in list order), then every patch, then every del, then the meta. Collection order alone is never a change.

INVERSE of a batch against the plan it was applied to: each op is inverted against the plan as it stood just before that op, and the inverses are listed in reverse order. put of a new id -> del; put over an existing thing -> put of the old thing; del of an existing thing -> put of the old thing; del of an absent thing -> nothing; patch -> patch restoring the old values of exactly the fields named in its f and d (old value in f; names the thing lacked go in d, sorted), nothing when the thing is absent; meta likewise over the plan's fields (collection names skipped). An inverse that would restore nothing is left out.
FILE FORMAT. 'vectors' is a list; each has 'kind', 'name' (unique), 'rule' (what it pins) and kind-specific fields:
jsonEqual: a, b, expect (boolean): jsonEqual(a, b).
plansEqual: a, b, expect (boolean): plansEqual(a, b).

apply: plan, ops, expect (plan): plansEqual(applyOps(plan, ops), expect). The expected collections are also listed in the exact order the rules give, for engines that check order too. applyOps must not change its inputs.
diff: before, after, expect (ops): diffPlans(before, after) equals expect op for op, in order, each op compared with jsonEqual. Also plansEqual(applyOps(before, expect), after) must hold.
invert: plan, ops, expect (ops): invertOps(plan, ops) equals expect op for op, in order (jsonEqual). Also plansEqual(applyOps(applyOps(plan, ops), expect), plan) must hold (the round trip).
rebase: confirmed, pending (a list of batches), remote (a batch), expect (plan): the view after the remote batch lands, that is applyOps over confirmed of remote, then each pending batch in order.
client: start {seq, plan}, steps. Run one client engine from the start snapshot; after each step check every key present in that step's 'expect' (keys left out are not checked). Steps:
{do:'local', cid, ops}: a local edit made of exactly these ops, given this cid. It joins the end of pending; the view gains it.

{do:'receive', seq, cid, by, ops}: a server ops frame. Apply ops to confirmed; seq becomes the larger of seq and the frame's seq; when cid names a pending batch, that batch leaves pending ('own' true). 'gap' is true when the frame's seq is more than the previous seq + 1.
{do:'refuse', cid}: an error frame naming that cid: the batch leaves pending, nothing else changes.
{do:'snapshot', seq, plan}: a fresh snapshot after joining again: it becomes confirmed and seq; 'resend' lists the pending cids, oldest first, to send again (pending is kept until echoed).
{do:'undo', cid}: undo this client's last own local edit not yet undone: its inverse (computed against the view it was made on) becomes a new local edit with this cid; 'sent' is its ops.

Step expect keys: seq (number), pending (cids, oldest first), confirmed (plan, plansEqual), view (plan, plansEqual: confirmed with pending applied), own, gap (booleans), resend (cids), sent (ops, compared op for op with jsonEqual).

vectors.name: numbers-by-value
vectors.rule: 1 equals 1.0 and 1.00e0

vectors.name: key-order-ignored
vectors.rule: objects compare by keys regardless of order, deeply

vectors.name: array-order-matters
vectors.rule: arrays compare element by element in order

vectors.name: null-is-not-absent
vectors.rule: a field holding null differs from an absent field

vectors.name: no-type-coercion
vectors.rule: a number never equals a string or a boolean

vectors.name: absent-collection-is-empty
vectors.rule: an absent collection equals an empty one; a non-array collection is empty too

vectors.name: collection-order-ignored
vectors.rule: collections compare by id regardless of order

vectors.name: meta-array-order-matters
vectors.rule: an array that is not a collection is meta and compares in order

vectors.name: put-new-appends
vectors.rule: a put of a new id appends it to the end of the collection

vectors.name: put-replaces-whole-in-place
vectors.rule: a put of an existing id replaces the whole thing in its place: fields missing from v are gone

vectors.name: put-creates-absent-collection
vectors.rule: a put into an absent collection creates it

vectors.name: put-into-non-array-collection
vectors.rule: a collection holding a non-array counts as empty; a put replaces it with a new array

vectors.name: every-collection
vectors.rule: all eleven collections take puts; a list of id-things outside the list is meta and untouched

vectors.name: patch-sets-fields
vectors.rule: a patch sets the fields in f and keeps the others

vectors.name: patch-deletes-with-d
vectors.rule: names in d are deleted; a name the thing lacks is fine

vectors.name: patch-f-then-d
vectors.rule: f is applied before d, so a name in both ends deleted

vectors.name: patch-missing-thing-ignored
vectors.rule: a patch on a thing that is gone does nothing

vectors.name: patch-missing-collection-ignored
vectors.rule: a patch into an absent collection does nothing

vectors.name: patch-never-touches-id
vectors.rule: 'id' in a patch's f or d is ignored

vectors.name: patch-replaces-nested-value
vectors.rule: a patch replaces a field's whole value: no deep merge

vectors.name: patch-null-is-a-value
vectors.rule: null in f is stored as null, not as a delete

vectors.name: patch-numbers-by-value
vectors.rule: numbers written as 2.50 or 1.0 are the numbers 2.5 and 1

vectors.name: del-removes
vectors.rule: a del removes the thing and keeps the others in order

vectors.name: del-missing-is-noop
vectors.rule: a del of a thing already gone does nothing

vectors.name: meta-sets-and-deletes
vectors.rule: meta sets f then deletes d on the plan's top-level fields

vectors.name: meta-ignores-collections
vectors.rule: collection names in a meta's f or d are ignored

vectors.name: meta-replaces-nested-value
vectors.rule: meta replaces a field's whole value, gtnhplanner included

vectors.name: batch-put-then-patch
vectors.rule: ops apply in order: a patch after a put lands on the new thing

vectors.name: batch-del-then-put-appends
vectors.rule: a put after a del of the same id is a new thing, appended at the end

vectors.name: batch-patch-after-del-ignored
vectors.rule: a patch after a del of the same thing does nothing

vectors.name: batch-later-write-wins
vectors.rule: two writes to one field in a batch: the later wins

vectors.name: empty-batch
vectors.rule: an empty batch changes nothing

vectors.name: diff-identical
vectors.rule: equal plans give an empty batch, even with keys reordered and numbers respelled

vectors.name: diff-reorder-only
vectors.rule: moving things around inside a collection is no change

vectors.name: diff-absent-vs-empty-collection
vectors.rule: an absent collection and an empty one are the same; no meta op for collections

vectors.name: diff-added-thing
vectors.rule: a thing only in after is a put of the whole thing

vectors.name: diff-removed-thing
vectors.rule: a thing only in before is a del

vectors.name: diff-changed-field
vectors.rule: a thing in both with a field changed is a patch of only that field, its whole new value

vectors.name: diff-removed-fields-sorted
vectors.rule: removed fields go in d, sorted by UTF-16 code units (capitals first); f stays, empty

vectors.name: diff-added-and-removed-fields
vectors.rule: one patch carries both the set fields and the deleted ones

vectors.name: diff-null-vs-absent
vectors.rule: a field going from absent to null is set to null; from a value to absent is a delete

vectors.name: diff-array-field-order
vectors.rule: an array inside a thing compares in order: reordered waypoints are a change

vectors.name: diff-meta
vectors.rule: changed top-level fields make one meta op: set in f, removed in d (sorted)

vectors.name: diff-batch-order
vectors.rule: every put (collections in list order), then every patch, then every del, then the meta

vectors.name: diff-thing-order
vectors.rule: puts and patches follow after's order; dels follow before's order

vectors.name: diff-collection-dropped
vectors.rule: a collection that disappears is a del of each thing in it, never a meta

vectors.name: diff-id-change
vectors.rule: a thing whose id changed is a put of the new id and a del of the old one

vectors.name: diff-meta-array
vectors.rule: an array of id-things outside the collection list is meta, sent whole

vectors.name: diff-task-moves
vectors.rule: task board edits are ordinary patches and puts

vectors.name: invert-put-new
vectors.rule: a put of a new thing inverts to a del

vectors.name: invert-put-existing
vectors.rule: a put over an existing thing inverts to a put of the old thing

vectors.name: invert-del
vectors.rule: a del inverts to a put of the old thing

vectors.name: invert-del-missing
vectors.rule: a del of a thing already gone inverts to nothing

vectors.name: invert-patch
vectors.rule: a patch inverts to a patch restoring exactly its fields: old values in f, fields that were absent in d

vectors.name: invert-patch-missing
vectors.rule: a patch on a thing that is gone inverts to nothing

vectors.name: invert-patch-same-name-twice
vectors.rule: a name in both f and d is restored once; 'id' is never restored

vectors.name: invert-meta
vectors.rule: meta inverts to meta restoring its fields; collection names are skipped

vectors.name: invert-sequential
vectors.rule: each op inverts against the plan just before it, and the inverses run in reverse order

vectors.name: invert-mixed-batch
vectors.rule: a diff-shaped batch inverts in reverse: meta first, then the dels' puts, patches, and the puts' dels last

vectors.name: invert-del-then-put
vectors.rule: a del followed by a put of the same id round-trips to the old thing

vectors.name: invert-empty
vectors.rule: an empty batch inverts to an empty batch

vectors.name: rebase-other-thing
vectors.rule: a remote edit to another thing shows beside the pending edit

vectors.name: rebase-same-field
vectors.rule: pending edits go on top: the own value shows until the server orders it

vectors.name: rebase-remote-delete
vectors.rule: a thing deleted remotely stays gone; the pending patch on it does nothing

vectors.name: rebase-two-pending
vectors.rule: several pending batches re-apply in order over the remote batch

vectors.name: client-echo-acks
vectors.rule: a local edit waits in pending until its own echo, which confirms it

vectors.name: client-remote-while-pending
vectors.rule: someone else's batch lands under the pending one; the echo then confirms the server's order

vectors.name: client-reconnect-resends
vectors.rule: after a reconnect the snapshot becomes confirmed and every pending batch is sent again, oldest first

vectors.name: client-duplicate-ack
vectors.rule: a batch the server already applied before the reconnect is acknowledged with no ops at the current seq

vectors.name: client-refused
vectors.rule: a refused batch leaves pending and the view

vectors.name: client-gap
vectors.rule: a seq that jumps past the next one reports a gap (join again for a snapshot)

vectors.name: client-undo-own-only
vectors.rule: undo sends the inverse of the own edit: only the fields it changed go back, others' edits stay

vectors.name: client-undo-overwrites
vectors.rule: undo restores the own field even when someone changed it since (Figma's rule)
